name: Julian Brush
preparty_markdown:
Julian became famous young and has been trying ever since to convince people that this is not the same thing

as becoming famous accidentally. His paintings are lush, moody, and highly collectible; his interviews are

less reliable. He is charming, vain in a way he almost gets away with, and genuinely serious about his work

when nobody is watching.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Warm, competitive, mercurial, self-aware enough to joke about his ego but not enough to lose it.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Long creative history with Imogen Muse.

• Malcolm Carrara thinks Julian gets too much press for work that can hang on a wall without engineering permits.

• Daphne Palette owns one of Julian's early paintings and mentions this strategically.

COSTUME

Black tie with artist flair: velvet jacket, open collar, paint-spattered vintage shoes, dramatic ring, scarf, or deliberately

imperfect formalwear.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“I was misunderstood before it was collectible.”

“That painting is from my early period, which is art-world language for 'please stop showing it.'”

Do not invent private history with Sterling Voss before game night. Your sealed party-night packet will reveal what your character actually knows

about him.

name: Helena Cross
preparty_markdown:
Helena is the lawyer museums call when an object has three owners, four countries, six contradictory export

documents, and one increasingly angry newspaper. She is elegant, surgical, and frighteningly good at making

a sentence mean exactly what she intends. Tonight she is attending as counsel to several parties who would

prefer not to be described as 'parties.'

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Precise, formidable, patient, amused by sloppy certainty. Ask pointed questions and answer only the question actually

asked.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Works regularly with Adrian Vellum and Margot Ledger.

• Friendly professional adversary of Vivienne Marrow; they have argued opposite sides of restitution cases and still have

dinner afterward.

• Marcus Pryce has supplied expert opinions for her cases.

COSTUME

Structured formalwear, crisp lines, minimal jewelry, immaculate folder or document case. Optional reading glasses for

dramatic removal.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“That is not illegal. It is merely a terrible idea.”

“I did not say you were wrong. I asked whether you could prove it.”

Do not invent private history with Sterling Voss before game night. Your sealed party-night packet will reveal what your character actually knows

about him.

name: Dr. Marcus Pryce
role: Professor of Art History & Provenance Scholar
preparty_markdown:
Marcus has built a career tracing the lives of objects through wars, estates, auctions, private collections, and

suspicious gaps in paperwork. Brilliant, argumentative, and allergic to oversimplification, he can turn one

stamp on the back of a frame into a forty-minute lecture and somehow make it compelling. Treasures of the

World contains several objects he has researched personally.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Intense, professorial, curious, occasionally pedantic, sincerely excited by evidence.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Supervises Sebastian Reed's doctoral research.

• Debates restitution policy regularly with Vivienne Marrow and Juno March.

• Rafael Gilt is one of the few people Marcus trusts to tell him when physical evidence contradicts his theory.

COSTUME

Professor at a donor gala: dark suit, tweed or textured jacket, distinctive glasses, scholarly scarf, pocket notebook. Optional

magnifier or archival pencil.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“There is no missing history. There is only history someone has misplaced.”

“I can explain it briefly or correctly.”

Do not invent private history with Sterling Voss before game night. Your sealed party-night packet will reveal what your character actually knows

about him.
